svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: gas exchange, photosynthesis and transpiration
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Light energy passes through the transparent cuticle and upper epidermis and is absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts, most of them in the palisade cells."], [3, "Carbon dioxide diffuses into the leaf through open stomata, across the substomatal air space and the air spaces of the spongy mesophyll, and dissolves in the moist walls of the mesophyll cells."], [7, "Water reaches the leaf in the xylem, moves into the mesophyll cells and evaporates from their walls into the air spaces. Water vapour diffuses out through the stomata: this is transpiration."], [10.5, "Oxygen made in photosynthesis diffuses out through the stomata. Sugar made in the mesophyll is loaded into the phloem as sucrose and carried to the rest of the plant."]]
svg.title: Transverse section of a leaf
svg.desc: A transverse section through a dicotyledonous leaf showing the waxy cuticle, upper epidermis, palisade mesophyll with chloroplasts, spongy mesophyll with air spaces, a vascular bundle with xylem above phloem inside a bundle sheath, and the lower epidermis with stomata between guard cells above substomatal air spaces.
svg.text: Part of the lamina of a dicot leaf, highly magnified. Cell contents simplified; not to scale.

g.data-info: Connected spaces between the spongy mesophyll cells that open to the outside through the stomata; carbon dioxide, oxygen and water vapour diffuse through them.
A thin, non-cellular layer of wax secreted by the epidermis. Waterproof: it reduces water loss by evaporation and is transparent, so light passes through. Thicker on the upper surface.
A single layer of flattened, transparent cells with no chloroplasts. Lets light through to the mesophyll and protects the tissues beneath.
Tall, column-shaped cells packed tightly near the upper surface, with many chloroplasts: the main site of photosynthesis. Their shape and position absorb as much light as possible.
Irregular, loosely packed cells with fewer chloroplasts. Their moist walls give a large surface for gas exchange with the air spaces.
A ring of tightly packed cells around the vein; substances pass through them between the vein and the mesophyll.
Xylem and phloem surrounded by a bundle sheath. Veins bring water and mineral ions to the leaf and carry sugars away, and support the lamina.
On the upper side of the vein: dead, hollow vessels with lignified walls that bring water and mineral ions into the leaf.
On the lower side of the vein: sieve tubes and companion cells that carry sucrose and amino acids out of the leaf to the rest of the plant.
A large air space just inside each stoma, linked to the air spaces of the spongy mesophyll.
A single layer of cells with a thin cuticle; it contains most of the stomata.
A pair of curved cells around each stoma. They contain chloroplasts. When they take up water and become turgid the stoma opens; when they lose water it closes.
A pore between two guard cells through which carbon dioxide diffuses in and oxygen and water vapour diffuse out. Plural: stomata.
Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis. Most numerous in the palisade cells; they can move towards the light.

svg.text: Key: CO₂ carbon dioxide · H₂O water · O₂ oxygen · suc sucrose

g.text: 1 Light is absorbed by chlorophyll in the palisade chloroplasts
2 Carbon dioxide diffuses in through the stomata and air spaces
3 Water from the xylem evaporates; water vapour diffuses out (transpiration)
4 Oxygen diffuses out; sucrose is loaded into the phloem
